RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for  ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday,  the April 16, 2008/Chaitra 27, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Defence; Earth Sciences; Home
Affairs; Information and Broadcasting; Labour and Employment;
Parliamentary Affairs; Rural Development; Science and
Technology; Textiles)
Total number of questions — 20
107
Restart of anti-migrant drive in
Maharashtra
*341. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA
A. HEPTULLA:
SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
 Will the Minister of  HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
anti-migrant drive has again been started
by the Maharashtra  Navnirman Sena
(MNS) activists against the workers of U.P.
and Bihar;
(b)  if so, how many cases have been
registered in Maharashtra against such
people disturbing peace and security and
how many have been arrested;
(c)  whether Government is also aware
that such drives are going on in various
places of Maharashtra;
(d)  if so, whether Government will
compensate the people who lost their jobs
in Maharashtra and were forced to board
the trains; and
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor?
Barbed wire fencing along
international border
*342. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of  HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a)  the length of barbed wire fencing
erected so far on the international border in
different States of the country;
(b)  the length that remains to be
completed, State-wise;
(c)  how many families have fallen
within Indian territory, but beyond fencing,
in different States;
(d) whether Government is pondering
over development schemes in the areas
falling beyond the fencing;
(e)  if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?

108
Gram Panchayats rallying points for
Job Cards under NREGS
*343. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANW ARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of  RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Gram Panchayats are now
becoming the rallying point  to issue Job-
Cards and giving work to the eligible rural
households, under the National Rural
Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS)
being implemented in 330 districts from
April, 2007;
(b)  if so, whether the requisite
infrastructure and expertise is available with
them;
(c)  whether the projects being executed
under this Scheme are identified by the
Panchayats;
(d)  whether any district/State level
guidelines exist; and
(e)  whether the assets being created
under this Scheme and the amount
disbursed, are being periodically monitored?
Reserved products  for SSIs
†*344. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI   RAM
JETHMALANI:
 Will the Minister of  COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY  be pleased to state:
(a)  whether  it is a fact that
manufacturing of only thirty five products
is  now in the reserved list for manufacturing
in the Small Scale Industry (SSI) sector;
(b)  if not, the facts in this regard;
(c)  the number of reserved products
for the SSI sector by March, 2004; and
(d)  the reasons for reducing the number
of reserved commodities for manufacturing
in SSI sector from March, 2004 to January,
2008?
Law on social security for workers
*345. SHRI  PENUMALLI MADHU:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government intends to
bring any law on social security for
workers as promised in the Common
Minimum Programme;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c)  if not, the reasons for not
implementing the pro-people social
security for workers as promised in the
Common Minimum Programme?
Indo-Pak Joint Group for export
strategy
*346. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a)  whether an Indo-Pak Joint Group
has been constituted to explore the
possibilities of coordinated export strategy
in potential areas;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c)  which are the special groups of trade
that  are proposed to be focussed?
Negative growth of apparel
exports
*347. SHRI NARESH GUJRAL: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

109
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
apparel exports are showing a negative
growth of 13 per cent as against a positive
growth of 32 per cent in 2005-06;
(b)  whether Government is also aware
that 6.8 lakh workers have lost their jobs in
this sector in the current year; and
(c)  if so, what fiscal steps Government
is taking to arrest this trend considering the
fact that the rupee has hardened by over 15
per cent against foreign currency?
Serial on freedom fighters
†*348. SHRI  JAI PARKASH
AGGARW AL: W ill the Minister of
INFORMATION AND BROAD-
CASTING be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government proposes to
broadcast or produce any serial based on
the biographies of prominent freedom
fighters;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c)  the names of the prominent freedom
fighters based on whose biographies serials
have been broadcast or produced during
the last three years, till date, year-wise/
Doordarshan Kendra-wise?
Amendment to the Industrial
Disputes Act, 1947
†*349. DR.   MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
 Will the Minister of  LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government has decided
to amend the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947;
(b)  if so, whether  this amendment will
enable industrialists to sack the workers
employed with them without any prior
notice;
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and
(d)  whether it is also a fact that in the
first phase this law will be applicable to
construction and textile industry of the
country?
Involvement of BSF officers in
smuggling
*350. SHRI  T.S. BAJW A: Will the
Minister of  HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
some Border Security Force (BSF) officers
are involved in smuggling in R.S. Pura Sector
(J &K), who were caught red handed; and
(b)  if so, the details of such officers and
the action taken by Government in this
regard to spot out those corrupt officers?
Measures to improve Indo-Pak trade
*351. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of  COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a)  whether India and Pakistan had
taken a host of measures in August, 2007
to improve trade relations and set a $10
billion bilateral trade target by 2010;
(b)  whether India has now plans to
prune its list of 884 sensitive items so as to
expand trade with Pakistan;
(c)  if so, the details of expansion/
opening of gates by India for more Pak
goods;
(d)  whether Indian trade officials,
however, feel that a positive list policy is
in gross violation of South Asian Free Trade
Agreement (SAFTA); and

110
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(e)  if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Crops damaged due to rains in Tamil
Nadu
*352. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of  HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
incessant rains claimed many lives and
caused an extensive damage to standing
crops in Tamil Nadu recently;
(b)  if so, the details thereof alongwith
the number of acres of crops including
paddy, cotton and other crops damaged due
to rains; and
(c)  the details of the assistance
provided by the Centre to the State?
Destruction of crops due to heavy
rains in States
*353. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of  HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether large scale destruction of
crops due to heavy rains has been reported
recently from various States;
(b)  if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has taken
steps to ascertain the loss due to the
calamity;
(d)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(e) the details of the measures taken
and relief/assistance sanctioned to the
States?
Plan to flush out Maoists from eight
naxal affected districts
*354. SHRI  RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
 Will the Minister of  HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a)  whether the Centre has picked up
eight naxal affected  districts in the country
including Malkangiri and Rayagada in
Orissa to flush out Maoists;
(b)  if so, the details thereof;
(c)  whether the Centre proposes to
deploy a joint Central Security Force to
tackle this menace; and
(d)  if so, the details thereof and the
time-frame within which this menace is
proposed to be controlled effectively?
Financing extremists under Surrender
and Rehabilitation Policy
†*355. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government has a scheme
of financing  extremists under its ‘Surrender
and Rehabilitation Policy’;
(b)  if so, the details of the above scheme
and the names of the States where it has
been introduced;
(c)  the year-wise and State-wise details
of the extremists who have surrendered
under the above scheme during the last three
years including the current year;
(d)  the details of the amount spent in
the above context; and
(e)  the details of those leading peaceful
life after the surrender?

111
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Broadcast of news and current affairs
by FM radio
*356. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will
the Minister of  INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government has been
disallowing news and current affairs
content on private FM radio till now,
despite persistent demand from the
industry;
(b)  whether a midway solution could
be found, if  a proposal from the Telecom
Regulatory Authority of India is accepted;
(c)  whether in a significant suggestion
in a consultation paper on the proposed
next phase of expansion of private FM radio
broadcasting TRAI has said that
broadcasters could be considered for certain
freedom and allowed to broadcast exactly
same news and current affairs contents
already aired by AIR and Doordarshan; and
(d)  whether any final decision has been
taken in this regard?
Women in Delhi threatened on phone
*357. SHRI MATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of  HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware of
the increasing number of cases where
women in Delhi have been threatened on
phone by known/unknown people;
(b)  whether Government is also aware
that Delhi Police is not taking such cases
seriously and that they have even refused
to register FIRs on the complaints of some
victims;
 (c)  whether any vigilance enquiry has
been conducted on the  complaints of such
victims in North-East District of Delhi
Police against the erring investigation
officers; and
(d)  if so, the outcome thereof and the
follow up action taken by the Department
in this regard?
Hindi speaking people killed in
Manipur
†*358. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of  HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Hindi
speaking persons have been killed by
terrorists in Manipur recently;
(b)  if so, the reasons for resorting to
killings by terrorists;
(c)  the stringent steps being taken by
Government to check recurrence of such
incidents; and
(d)  whether any action plan has been
made to provide security to Hindi speaking
persons residing in North-Eastern States?
Allowing farmers to develop their own
fields under NREGS
*359. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI:
 Will the Minister of  RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government has favoured
the extension of the National Rural
Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS)
to enable the farmers to develop their own
fields;
(b)  whether to include the farmers under
the NREGS to work on their own fields is
a new idea and can be considered; and
(c)  if so, whether any final decision in
this regard has been taken and whether

112
Members of Parliament also recommended
to extend the NREGS to the farmers?
Losses due to rains in southern States
*360. SHRI  RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister
of  HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that heavy rains
lashed the southern Indian States during
March this year, which caused heavy losses
both of human lives and property;
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State-
wise;
(c)  whether any Central assistance has
been given to the States for the losses
suffered; and
(d)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise
and the basis thereof?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 10th April, 2008 Secretary-General.
Chaitra 21, 1930 (Saka)
